nodes.name: Substrate cleaning
nodes.procedure: Mild steel substrates were cleaned by electro-cleaning process, by dipping in H2SO4 for 2 min at 30 vol% (acid dip process). After each precleaning process, the substrates were rinsed with DI water.
nodes.source_text: The substrates were cleaned by electro-cleaning process, by dipping in H2SO4 for 2 min at 30 vol% (acid dip process). After each precleaning process, the substrates were rinsed with DI water.

nodes.name: NiCu electrodeposition 5A/cm²
nodes.procedure: Nickel sulphate (NiSO4.6H2O), copper sulphate (CuSO4.6H2O), and Trisodium citrate were used for the bath composition. Mild steel (pre-cleaned) was used as cathode and nickel bar as anode in a two-electrode cell. NiCu alloy thin film was electrodeposited using pulse electrodeposition (galvanostatic method) at current density of 5 A/cm² for 15 min.
nodes.source_text: NiCu alloy was electrodeposited using the pulse electrodeposition method with a current density of 5 A/cm² ... for 15 min.

nodes.name: NiCu electrodeposition 10A/cm²
nodes.procedure: After the successful preparation of the bath composition containing Nickel sulphate (NiSO4.6H2O), copper sulphate (CuSO4.6H2O), and Trisodium citrate, thin films of NiCu were fabricated using the electrodeposition technique. Under the galvanostatic method, the thin films were fabricated in a two-electrode cell set with mild steel as the cathode and nickel bar as an anode using pulse electrodeposition method with a current density of 10 A/cm² for 15 min.
nodes.source_text: NiCu alloy was electrodeposited using the pulse electrodeposition method with a current density of 10 A/cm² ... for 15 min.

nodes.source_text: the thin films were fabricated in a two-electrode cell set with varying current density and temperatures of 50°C ... NiCu alloy was electrodeposited using the pulse electrodeposition method with a current density of 15 A/cm²@50°C for 15 min.

nodes.name: NiCu electrodeposition 15A/cm²@70°C
nodes.procedure: After the successful preparation of the bath composition containing Nickel sulphate (NiSO4.6H2O), copper sulphate (CuSO4.6H2O), and Trisodium citrate, thin films of NiCu were fabricated using the electrodeposition technique. Under the galvanostatic method, the thin films were fabricated in a two-electrode cell set with varying current density and temperatures of 70°C, in which mild steel was used as the cathode and nickel bar was used as an anode. NiCu alloy was electrodeposited using the pulse electrodeposition method with a current density of 15 A/cm²@70°C for 15 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu samples at 5, 10, 15 A/cm² show cubic crystal system (ICSD 98-008-7502) with peaks at 45.1° (111) and 52.6° (002); peak intensity and crystallinity increase with deposition current. Strains: 1.755×10⁻³, 4.539×10⁻³, 5.626×10⁻³ for 5, 10, 15 A/cm² respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1 shows the XRD analysis of the NiCu samples with varying deposition currents of 5, 10 and 15 Acm². Reasonable peaks were observed at 45.1° and 52.6° which correspond to hkl values of 111 and 002 respectively of the samples ... A strain of about 1.755, 4.539, and 5.626×10⁻³ was found which clearly shows the reason for the peak shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu 15 A/cm² exhibits agglomerated cauliflower-like particle morphology confirmed by SEM and FESEM at low/high magnification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It was observed from Fig. 2 a and b show the SEM analysis of the fabricated film at 15 A/cm² that the particles were agglomerated and cauliflower-like morphology was observed ... agglomerated cauliflower-like morphology was observed which further confirms the morphology of the SEM analysis with FESEM analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-PSTAT NiCu-15 A/cm² shows increased peak intensity and crystallinity with additional K peaks; strain 9.565×10⁻³ due to K⁺ intercalation/deintercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S11 shows the images of comparative NiCu 15 A/cm² film before and after PSTAT analysis. After PSTAT analysis an increase in the peak was observed ... A strain of about 9.565×10⁻³ was found.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-PSTAT NiCu-15 A/cm² shows extensive grain growth with cubic crystal structure developing into rod morphology due to harsh anodization/cathodization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S12 clearly shows that extensive growth was observed after PSTAT analysis, which is due to the harsh anodization and cathodization. The cubic crystal structure had grown as a rod observed in Fig. S12.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-PSTAT NiCu-15 A/cm² confirms Ni, Cu, C, K presence; Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ at 853.5/871.7 eV, Ni³⁺ at 855.5/873.3 eV; Cu 2p shows Cu²⁺ states; K 2p at 292.4/295.2 eV confirms K⁺ trapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 7 shows the XPS spectrum which confirms the presence of Ni, Cu, C and K in NiCu alloy film ... Fig. 7d shows the high-resolution spectrum of the K 2p spectrum ... peaks at 292.4 eV correspond to 2p3/2 and ... 295.2 eV correspond to 2p1/2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-PSTAT NiCu-15 A/cm² shows cauliflower-like morphology with extensive grain growth, lattice fringes 0.14 nm (ICSD 98-008-7502), same cubic structure, compressive strain -6.085%. HAADF confirms Ni, Cu purity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 8(a-b) shows the images taken at lower and higher magnifications of the NiCu sample after PSTAT ... Fig. 8c shows the indexed lattice fringes ... fringe width of the lattice was 0.14 nm ... An increase in the compressive strain of about -6.085% was calculated.
